scope: read_selected pass cache and adaptive fallback
observations: Auto remains exhaustive/default; never/always remain named one-polarity reads.
Adaptive fallback is selector-specific; a found confident target can legitimately skip inversion and miss unrelated text.
Adaptive response cache includes selector/index/fuzzy; polarity caches retain complete raw words until merge to preserve legacy auto quality.
No testing.find/action, runtime input or screen.marks defaults were switched to adaptive.

limits: Selected hand-labelled target subset, not a random production distribution or exhaustive transcription
Only installed eng language model; accented Latin targets remain difficult and were not accent-normalized into apparent successes
Three timing trials per case/mode; normal OS caching and concurrent host load are uncontrolled
Equality of labelled recall on these16images does not prove equal recognition coverage on other screens
MCP microsequence is a functional/cache observation, not a3-run latency distribution
Payload savings describe this target query, not arbitrary screenshots
No device capture/transfer, input latency, agent reasoning, PhoneUse or FPS comparison
recommendations: Keep auto default for broad text/ambiguity-sensitive tasks; expose adaptive only as an explicit target-query speed tradeoff.
Never treat a confident single-pass target as evidence that all other labels or duplicate controls were seen.
Use fresh image/ROI and explicit selector; keep all matches and refuse ambiguous input rather than choosing index0 implicitly.
Retain target-miss/empty/low-confidence fallback and keep recognizer invocation counters separate from logical pass counts.
Document local read timings separately from capture/transport; judge speed and full labelled recall together.
historical_only: qa/ocr-fast/candidate-debug-raw.json used an earlier all-words confidence guard and a debug build; it is excluded from final performance evidence
